scan_notes: Reviewed the branch diff and log, traced the registry through picker, page resolution, review, baseline, and workbook consumers, and checked the upgraded-schema and autocommit assumptions. Canonical product-code guards and demo precedence are consistently enforced in the live serving seams. Fact-check and structural normalization/serving tests passed; database-backed tests could not run because the sandbox denied local PostgreSQL connections.

findings.title: Workbook can combine registry and pointer data from different snapshots
findings.evidence: `state = _pointer_state(conn)` and `tenants = client_registry.tenants(conn)` execute as separate statements on an autocommit connection.
findings.failure_scenario: A tenant has product code `ACME` and published pointers. The workbook reads pointer state keyed by `ACME`; then `tenant update --slug acme --product-code ACME2` commits before the registry read. The registry returns `ACME2`, but `state` contains only `ACME`, so the generated workbook falsely reports the tenant's slots as having nothing published even though those pointers now serve through `ACME2`.
findings.suggested_fix: Read pointer state and tenants inside one `conn.read_only_snapshot()` transaction, or fetch both through a single statement keyed by stable client ID.

overall_explanation: No—there is one remaining behavioral defect, not merely debatable wording. The live picker and serving seams otherwise appear consistent, including malformed-row quarantine, canonical-code enforcement, and demo precedence.
